common_name: Cherry Dazzle Crapemyrtle (Very Compact Cherry-Red Dwarf Crape Myrtle)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Cherry Dazzle is part of the Razzle Dazzle series of true dwarf crape myrtles bred for compact, mounded landscape use.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Cherry Dazzle is a true dwarf crape myrtle from the Razzle Dazzle series, staying under 3 feet tall even at maturity, and bears vivid cherry-red flower clusters from summer into fall on a dense, mounded shrub that needs no pruning to control size, unlike full-size crape myrtles that are often cut back hard each winter. Its compact scale suits foundation plantings, low hedges, and mixed borders where a full-size crape myrtle would quickly outgrow the space. Deadhead spent flower clusters to encourage continued reblooming through the season, and prune only lightly in late winter to remove dead or crossing wood.

common_name: Delta Flame Crapemyrtle (Fire-Engine Red Dark-Foliage Crape Myrtle)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Delta Flame is a Southern Living Plant Collection crapemyrtle bred for dark maroon-purple foliage and vivid red blooms.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Delta Flame bears vivid, fire-engine-red flower clusters that stand out sharply against dark maroon-purple foliage, a bold contrast maintained through the heat of a Gulf South summer, on a medium-sized landscape shrub or small tree. It is heat-tolerant and generally resists deer browsing better than many other landscape shrubs. Deadhead spent flower clusters to encourage continued reblooming through the season, and prune lightly in late winter to remove only dead, crossing, or downward-growing branches rather than heavily topping the plant.

common_name: Delta Eclipse Crapemyrtle (Deep Magenta Dark-Foliage Crape Myrtle)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Delta Eclipse is a Southern Living Plant Collection crapemyrtle bred for near-black foliage and deep magenta-pink blooms.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Delta Eclipse bears rich, deep magenta-pink flower clusters against near-black purple foliage, one of the darkest foliage colors available among crape myrtle cultivars, creating dramatic contrast through the heat of a Gulf South summer on a medium-sized landscape shrub or small tree. It is heat-tolerant and generally resists deer browsing better than many other landscape shrubs. Deadhead spent flower clusters to encourage continued reblooming through the season, and prune lightly in late winter to remove only dead, crossing, or downward-growing branches rather than heavily topping the plant.

common_name: Subcostata Crape Myrtle (Cold-Hardy Species with Exfoliating Bark)

planting.note: Plant container trees in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Lagerstroemia subcostata is a cold-hardy crape myrtle species grown primarily for its outstanding exfoliating bark.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Lagerstroemia subcostata is grown chiefly for its outstanding ornamental bark, which peels away in patches to reveal a smooth, mottled tapestry of cinnamon, gray, and cream tones, providing four-season interest that outshines its relatively modest clusters of small white summer flowers. It is notably more cold-hardy than most ornamental crape myrtle hybrids and has been used as breeding stock to pass improved bark quality and cold tolerance into modern cultivars. Site it where the trunk can be seen and appreciated year-round, such as near a patio or entry, and prune only to remove dead or crossing branches, since heavy pruning sacrifices the multi-trunked form that best displays the bark.

common_name: Lime-Bark Crape Myrtle (Uncommon Smooth Pale-Bark Species)

planting.note: Plant container trees in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Lagerstroemia limii is an uncommon crape myrtle species grown chiefly for its smooth, pale, flaking bark.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Lagerstroemia limii is an uncommon species crape myrtle valued primarily for its smooth, pale bark that flakes away in thin patches to reveal lighter tones beneath, a subtler bark effect than the boldly mottled trunks of subcostata or fauriei types, paired with modest clusters of small white summer flowers. Its rarity in cultivation makes it more a collector's specimen than a mainstream landscape plant, best suited to gardeners specifically seeking species-level crape myrtle diversity beyond the common indica and fauriei hybrids. Site it where the trunk can be appreciated, and prune only to remove dead or crossing branches to preserve the multi-trunked form that shows off the bark.
